newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria places 2.6 bln levs 1-wk discount T-bills.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria places 2.6 bln levs 1-wk discount T-bills.

text.p: Bulgaria's finance ministry placed 2.64 billion levs worth of one-week discount T-bills, yielding 3.15 percent until maturity, the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said.
In line with its usual practice the BNB did not say with which financial institutions the issue was placed on Thursday.
Details of the issue follow. Price is in percent of par:
On Wednesday the ministry placed another T-bill issue with the same parameters and a par of 7.22 billion levs.

The ministry has said recently it planned to cover interest and maturity payments on government securities with rolloever issues of treasury paper after domestic debt surged due to record high central interest rates.
The BNB's central interest rate is now set at 15 percent monthly or 180 percent annually after 300 percent in September and 240 percent in October.
Bulgaria's domestic debt rose by 171 billion levs to 893.3 billion levs in November due to a fall in the lev and new government securities issues placed to bridge the budget gap.

The fall in the lev boosted the lev price of the two types of dollar-denominated government bonds issued by the Finance Ministry to cover bad debts of state enterprises to banks and to compensate creditors in bankrupt banks respectively.
